freeText.question: How do you pronounce your name?
Why do you want to work at Anthropic?
freeText.answer:
I want to work at Anthropic because the role combines rigorous software engineering with practical work that helps people use advanced AI responsibly. I have spent more than five years building and operating financial-services software, approaching six years, where reliability, failure handling, performance, and clear operational feedback matter every day. Alongside this production engineering work, I developed a Hybrid Social Group Optimization method for COVID-19 detection from chest X-ray images, achieving over 99% accuracy, and published the work in the peer-reviewed Cognitive Computation journal. That experience gave me a strong appreciation for empirical evaluation, careful problem decomposition, and communicating technical work clearly.

At ION Group, I also worked on event-driven systems, improved a Java component's performance through multithreading, reduced production issue-analysis time through log analysis, and built recovery improvements for halted processing. In my personal work, I built an agentic personal assistant using free NVIDIA models and a coding harness. It maintains ideas and notes through natural-language chat, helps plan tasks and days, and is accessible from a phone through messenger apps 24/7. The Beneficial Deployments team is compelling because it treats applied AI as an engineering and enablement problem: understanding real constraints, evaluating systems, helping teams ship, and creating reusable tooling. I would bring a production-minded backend perspective, research experience, strong debugging instincts, and practical agentic-AI experience while continuing to deepen my work in evaluation, context engineering, and production deployment.

freeText.question: Additional Information
freeText.answer: My background is in production financial-services engineering, with strengths in Java, distributed/event-driven systems, performance optimization, database reliability, observability, machine-learning projects, and hands-on agentic AI work. My personal assistant project uses free NVIDIA models and a coding harness to maintain notes and ideas and plan tasks through messenger apps. I would be glad to discuss how these foundations translate to evaluation, agent architecture, and partner enablement work.
